descripcion_es: Connectors of cause, consequence, contrast, addition and order.
resumen: Words that link ideas and give coherence to a text or an oral presentation: to add, to contrast, to explain causes and consequences and to put things in order.

explicacion.texto: Look at what comes after each connector: because, although and so are followed by a clause (subject + verb); because of, despite and in spite of are followed by a noun or an -ing form. However and therefore usually go at the start of the sentence, followed by a comma.

filas: and / also / too
Addition: joins ideas / adds an extra one (es: y / también)
She speaks French and also German.
as well as
Addition: in addition to (es: además de)
As well as being cheap, it's fast.
moreover / what's more
Addition: furthermore (formal / informal) (es: además)
Moreover, the plan is too expensive.
in addition (to)
Addition: as well (as) (es: además (de))
In addition to the salary, there's a bonus.
but
Contrast: introduces an opposing idea (es: pero)
It's small but comfortable.
however
Contrast: nevertheless (es: sin embargo)
It's cheap. However, it's not very good.
although / even though
Contrast: despite the fact that (es: aunque)
Although it was raining, we went out.
despite / in spite of
Contrast: regardless of (es: a pesar de)
Despite the rain, we went out.
whereas / while
Contrast: compares two different facts (es: mientras que)
I like tea, whereas my wife prefers coffee.
on the other hand
Contrast: introduces the other side of an argument (es: por otro lado)
On the other hand, it's very noisy.
because
Cause: for the reason that (+ clause) (es: porque)
I stayed home because I was ill.
because of / due to
Cause: as a result of (+ noun) (es: debido a)
The flight was cancelled because of the fog.
since / as
Cause: given that (es: como, ya que)
As it was late, we took a taxi.
so
Consequence: and for that reason (es: así que)
I was tired, so I went to bed.
therefore / as a result
Consequence: for that reason / consequently (es: por tanto / como resultado)
Sales fell. As a result, prices dropped.
first(ly) / second(ly)
Order: introduces the first / second point (es: en primer / segundo lugar)
Firstly, let me introduce myself.
then / after that
Order: next / afterwards (es: luego / después de eso)
Then we had lunch.
finally / lastly
Order: introduces the last point (es: por último)
Finally, I'd like to thank you all.
for example / for instance / such as
Example: introduces examples (es: por ejemplo / como)
Some fruits, such as oranges, are rich in vitamin C.
in conclusion / to sum up
Conclusion: introduces a summary (es: en conclusión / en resumen)
To sum up, the results are positive.

items: Despite does not take of: despite the rain, not “despite of”.
Actually means “in fact, in reality”, not Spanish “actualmente” (currently, nowadays).
Eventually means “in the end, over time”, not Spanish “eventualmente” (possibly, occasionally).

ejemplos.frase: Although she was nervous, she gave an excellent presentation.
ejemplos.traduccion: Aunque estaba nerviosa, hizo una presentación excelente.

ejemplos.frase: The match was postponed because of the storm.
ejemplos.traduccion: El partido se aplazó por la tormenta.

ejemplos.frase: The house is lovely. On the other hand, it's far from the station.
ejemplos.traduccion: La casa es preciosa. Por otro lado, está lejos de la estación.

ejemplos.frase: We missed the train, so we had to wait an hour.
ejemplos.traduccion: Perdimos el tren, así que tuvimos que esperar una hora.

ejemplos.frase: Firstly, I'll describe the problem; then, I'll suggest some solutions.
ejemplos.traduccion: En primer lugar describiré el problema; luego propondré algunas soluciones.

ejemplos.frase: In spite of his age, my grandfather still runs every morning.
ejemplos.traduccion: A pesar de su edad, mi abuelo todavía corre todas las mañanas.

ejemplos.frase: Actually, I've never been to Paris.
ejemplos.traduccion: En realidad, nunca he estado en París.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Despite of the traffic, we arrived on time.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Despite does not take of; in spite of does.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The game was cancelled because the rain.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The game was cancelled because of the rain.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Before a noun you use because of.
Spanish “actualmente” is currently or at present; actually means “in fact”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Although it was cold, but we swam.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Although it was cold, we swam.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Although and but are not combined in the same sentence.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with because, because of or due to.
ejercicios.frase: The road was closed ___ the snow.
respuestas: because of
due to
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's rule on what comes after the connector: because goes with a clause and because of with a noun. The clue is the snow, a noun with no verb. That is why because of is needed; due to, from the same table row, also goes with a noun and is accepted with the same meaning. Because on its own, however, is not correct.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a noun (the snow) you use because of.
ejercicios.traduccion: La carretera estaba cortada debido a la nieve.

errores_previstos.respuesta: because
errores_previstos.explicacion: Because needs a clause with a verb (because it snowed); before a noun you use because of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: because for
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “por”: the correct preposition is of, because of.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the simplest connector of consequence.
ejercicios.frase: It was very late, ___ we took a taxi.
respuestas: so
ejercicios.explicacion: It is so, the simplest connector of consequence in the table. The clue is the logical relationship (it was late, so we took a taxi) and the comma after the first clause, which, as the card says, comes before so. Therefore also expresses consequence, but it is formal and usually starts a new sentence.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: So introduces a consequence and comes after a comma.
ejercicios.traduccion: Era muy tarde, así que cogimos un taxi.

errores_previstos.respuesta: because
errores_previstos.explicacion: Because introduces the cause, not the consequence; it would say that it was late because we took a taxi.

errores_previstos.respuesta: then
errores_previstos.explicacion: Then shows order in time (next), not consequence.

errores_previstos.respuesta: but
errores_previstos.explicacion: But expresses contrast; here the second idea is a consequence of the first.

ejercicios.frase: In ___ of the bad weather, the festival was a success.
respuestas: spite
ejercicios.explicacion: It is the contrast expression in spite of from the table. The clue is the structure In ___ of + noun (the bad weather), which only allows spite. In spite of and despite mean the same, but only in spite of takes of.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “a pesar de” is in spite of.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar del mal tiempo, el festival fue un éxito.

errores_previstos.respuesta: despite
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite does not take in or of; here the structure In ___ of requires spite.

errores_previstos.respuesta: spit
errores_previstos.explicacion: The final e is missing: spite. Spit means to force saliva out of your mouth.

ejercicios.frase: Some sports, such ___ tennis, can be played all year round.
respuestas: as
ejercicios.explicacion: It is such as from the examples table, used to introduce examples within the sentence. The clue is such before the gap: the fixed expression is such as. Such like or such how do not exist with this meaning.
ejercicios.traduccion: Algunos deportes, como el tenis, pueden practicarse todo el año.

errores_previstos.respuesta: like
errores_previstos.explicacion: Like can introduce examples (sports like tennis), but after such only as is correct.

errores_previstos.respuesta: how
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “como”: how refers to manner, it does not work for examples.

ejercicios.frase: ___ he studied hard, he failed the exam.
respuestas: Although
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's rule: although is followed by a clause (subject + verb) and expresses contrast. The clue is he studied hard, a complete clause, and the logical contrast between studying and failing. Despite would go with a noun or -ing, and because would say the opposite.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a complete clause, with a meaning of contrast: although.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque estudió mucho, suspendió el examen.

por_opcion.Although: Correct: although, followed by a complete clause with a verb.
por_opcion.Despite: Incorrect: despite goes with a noun or -ing (despite studying hard), not with a clause.
por_opcion.Because: Incorrect: it would say that he failed because he studied, which makes no sense.

ejercicios.frase: ___ the noise, I managed to sleep.
respuestas: Despite
ejercicios.explicacion: It is the rule that complements the previous one: despite is followed by a noun or -ing. The clue is the noise, a noun with no verb, and the contrast between the noise and managing to sleep. Despite does not take of.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a noun, with a meaning of contrast: despite.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar del ruido, conseguí dormir.

por_opcion.Despite: Correct: despite, followed by a noun.
por_opcion.Although: Incorrect: although needs a clause with a verb (although it was noisy).
por_opcion.However: Incorrect: however is an adverb that starts a sentence with a comma and cannot be followed by a noun.

ejercicios.frase: The hotel was noisy. ___, the service was poor.
respuestas: Moreover
ejercicios.explicacion: It is moreover from the addition table, used in a formal register. The clue is that both sentences go in the same direction: two complaints about the hotel. However would introduce a contrast and therefore a consequence, and neither exists here.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Another negative argument is added: moreover.
ejercicios.traduccion: El hotel era ruidoso. Además, el servicio era malo.

por_opcion.Moreover: Correct: it adds a second negative argument.
por_opcion.However: Incorrect: it would announce something positive in contrast with the noise.
por_opcion.Therefore: Incorrect: it shows consequence; the bad service is not a consequence of the noise.

ejercicios.frase: My brother loves the city, ___ I prefer the countryside.
respuestas: whereas
ejercicios.explicacion: It is whereas from the table, used to contrast two facts or preferences. The clue is the opposition between the city and the countryside, attributed to two different people. Whereas joins two complete clauses and usually comes after a comma.
ejercicios.traduccion: A mi hermano le encanta la ciudad, mientras que yo prefiero el campo.

por_opcion.whereas: Correct: it contrasts the preferences of two people.
por_opcion.so: Incorrect: so shows consequence; my preference is not a consequence of my brother's.
por_opcion.because: Incorrect: because shows cause; there is no causal relationship between the two tastes.

ejercicios.frase: Despite of the cost, they bought the house.
respuestas: Despite the cost, they bought the house.
In spite of the cost, they bought the house.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's list and its typical mistakes say it: despite does not take of. The clue is “Despite of”, a calque of Spanish “a pesar de”. There are two valid corrections: remove of (Despite the cost) or complete the other expression (In spite of the cost).
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar del coste, compraron la casa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite of the cost, they bought the house.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: despite never takes of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Spite of the cost, they bought the house.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In is missing: the full expression is in spite of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although the cost, they bought the house.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although needs a clause with a verb, not a noun.

ejercicios.enunciado: Correct the false friend so that it means “I currently live in Seville, but I'm moving next month”.
ejercicios.frase: Actually I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
respuestas: Currently I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
Currently, I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
At present I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
At present, I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
At the moment I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
At the moment, I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is the false friend the card points out: actually means “in fact”, not Spanish “actualmente”. The clue is the contrast with I'm moving next month, which requires the meaning “at this moment”. You must replace it with currently, at present or at the moment; all are correct, with or without a comma.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Actually means “in fact”; Spanish “actualmente” is currently, at present or at the moment.
ejercicios.traduccion: Actualmente vivo en Sevilla, pero me mudo el mes que viene.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Actually I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: actually means “in fact”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Actualy I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Besides not correcting the false friend, it is misspelt.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Eventually I live in Seville, but I'm moving next month.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Eventually is another false friend: it means “in the end, over time”.

ejercicios.frase: Although it was expensive, but I bought it.
respuestas: Although it was expensive, I bought it.
It was expensive, but I bought it.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card lists this typical mistake: although and but are not combined in the same sentence. In Spanish, “aunque… pero” is also incorrect, even though you hear it. There are two ways to correct it: keep although and remove but, or remove although and keep but.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Although and but are not combined in the same sentence.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although it was expensive, but I bought it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: although and but do not go together.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite it was expensive, I bought it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite cannot go with a clause; it would need despite the price or despite it being expensive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Join the two sentences with because of.
ejercicios.frase: We couldn't play. There was heavy rain.
respuestas: We couldn't play because of the heavy rain.
We couldn't play because of heavy rain.
We could not play because of the heavy rain.
We couldn't play because of the rain.
We could not play because of heavy rain.
We could not play because of the rain.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule because of + noun. To join the sentences you must turn the clause There was heavy rain into a noun: the heavy rain (or heavy rain, or the rain). That noun goes after because of, with no verb.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Because of is followed by a noun: the heavy rain.
ejercicios.traduccion: No pudimos jugar a causa de la lluvia intensa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We couldn't play because of there was heavy rain.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Because of does not allow a clause with a verb; you must keep only the noun.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We couldn't play because the heavy rain.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Before a noun you need because of, not because on its own.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence starting with Although.
ejercicios.frase: It was cold, but we went to the beach.
respuestas: Although it was cold, we went to the beach.
ejercicios.explicacion: Although replaces but and is placed before the first clause, the one that expresses the obstacle. As the card says, although and but are not combined, so but disappears. The two clauses are separated by a comma.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Although replaces but and goes before the first clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque hacía frío, fuimos a la playa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although it was cold, but we went to the beach.
errores_previstos.explicacion: When you add although, you must remove but.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although we went to the beach, it was cold.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although must go with the obstacle (it was cold), not with what was done.

respuestas: To sum up the results are positive
ejercicios.explicacion: It is to sum up from the conclusion table. It opens the sentence and is followed by the main clause: subject (the results) + verb (are) + complement (positive). It is one of the most useful formulas for closing an oral presentation.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To sum up introduces the conclusion.
ejercicios.traduccion: En resumen, los resultados son positivos.

errores_previstos.respuesta: To up sum the results are positive
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is to sum up, with up at the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: To sum up the positive results are
errores_previstos.explicacion: After the connector, the order is subject + verb + complement: the results are positive.

ejercicios.frase: Prices have risen sharply. ___, many families are spending less.
respuestas: As a result
ejercicios.explicacion: It is as a result from the consequence table. The clue is the cause-and-effect relationship between the two sentences (rising prices and less spending) and the comma after the gap, at the start of a new sentence. Because of would need a noun and although expresses contrast.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A consequence is expressed: as a result.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los precios han subido mucho. Como resultado, muchas familias gastan menos.

por_opcion.As a result: Correct: it introduces the consequence at the start of a new sentence.
por_opcion.Although: Incorrect: it expresses contrast and cannot be followed by a comma like this.
por_opcion.Because of: Incorrect: it needs a noun after it and expresses cause, not consequence.

descripcion_larga_es: Basic connectors link ideas and give coherence to what you say or write: they add (moreover), contrast (although, despite), explain causes and consequences (because of, so, as a result), put things in order (firstly, finally) and conclude (to sum up). Without them a text looks like a list of separate sentences. Spanish speakers find it hard to remember what comes after each one (a clause or a noun) and fall into false friends such as actually.

contexto.que_es: They are words or expressions that relate clauses and ideas: addition, contrast, cause, consequence, order, example and conclusion. Each one has its own grammar: because, although and so go with a clause (subject + verb); because of, despite and in spite of, with a noun or an -ing form; however and therefore start a sentence followed by a comma.
contexto.por_que_importa: Coherence and cohesion are explicit assessment criteria in any writing or speaking exam from B1 level. A badly chosen connector changes the logic of the message (although versus because) and a badly built one (despite of, because the rain) is very noticeable. The false friends actually and eventually cause real misunderstandings.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: In essays, emails, presentations and any kind of argument. The signal for choosing is twofold: the logical relationship between the ideas (adding, contrasting, cause, consequence) and what comes after (a complete clause or a noun). Spanish speakers tend to calque “a pesar de” as despite of and to use “porque” as because before nouns.
